parts.note: reads like a commander of an armed service, but the service meant is serving at table in a restaurant

explanation.surface: A question about who heads one of the armed services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests the army, navy or air force; here it is restaurant service, whose chief is the person in charge of the waiting staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior waiter runs the dining-room service, so is its chief in a cryptic sense.

definitions.meaning: the public that reads, listens or watches: the people a performance or book reaches
in theatre, the house is the people in the seats, as in 'a full house'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Public house' looks like a pub; split it into two separate definitions of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a reading public and a theatre house are names for the gathered spectators or listeners.

indicators.note: the fish's name goes around the next word, which sits inside it

parts.note: a bass is a fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone fishing about in the reservoirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish around' reads as someone searching, but the fish is the container and 'around' signals the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Basins are hollows or tanks holding water, as reservoirs do.

definitions.meaning: friendly means warm and kindly in manner
a type is a sort or category, as in 'of that sort'

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for warmth of manner and a noun for a sort or category.

clue.text: It can be hell for criminals

definitions.meaning: in myth, the realm of the dead below the earth, which may be hell
organised criminals considered as a whole society

explanation.surface: Life is a hell for people who break the law.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests prison as hell for criminals; in fact two senses of the word are given, joined by 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical realm below the earth and the criminal fraternity share this one name.

clue.text: Cast my anchor in Norway, say

indicators.note: to cast is to throw, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor drops anchor in a Norwegian harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a sailor dropping anchor but signals rearranging MYANCHOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway has a king as head of state, so it is an example of this form of government.

parts.note: reads as elite troops, but 'highly' means trained high up, in the mountains

explanation.surface: A question about Italy's elite troops.
explanation.walkthrough: These are Italy's mountain troops, trained among the Alps, so 'highly trained' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy's specialist mountain infantry regiments are named after the Alps where they train.

parts.note: SP, the starting price, is the betting odds at the start of a race
in cricket the batting side is 'in'

explanation.surface: A cricket bet on which team is batting.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker and billiards 'side' is spin put on the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In cue sports, side is the spin applied by striking the ball off-centre.

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A painting by old masters has been sold at auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'masters' suggests great painters; here they are schoolmasters, whose work is teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Schoolmasters' job is teaching pupils, which is what the word names.

parts.note: taken as written
to dock a tail is to cut it short, to lop it

explanation.surface: A choice between a ship's deck and the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' looks nautical like 'Deck' but is the verb meaning cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the lowest deck of a sailing ship.

indicators.note: the clue tells us the word wanted reads the same in both directions

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A word that reads the same both ways has been made immortal.
explanation.definitionFit: To deify someone is to make them a god, and gods are immortal.

clue.text: Delight in storytelling right from the start

indicators.note: the letter is taken away from the beginning of the word

parts.note: a relation is a telling or narration of a story

explanation.surface: Joy found in telling stories right from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right from the start' reads as 'from the very beginning', but means R taken off the front of RELATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is a feeling of great joy, a synonym for delight.

clue.text: She takes a long time to grasp the point

indicators.note: to grasp is to hold, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: ages means a long time
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A slow learner takes ages to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point, here N.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name stands for any woman, so 'She' defines it.

clue.text: He called to give the news

definitions.text: He called to give the news

parts.words: He called to give the news
parts.note: a man who called out public announcements in the streets

explanation.surface: Someone telephoned to pass on news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called' suggests a visit or phone call, but means shouting out proclamations in a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Before newspapers, an official shouted announcements in the streets of a town.

clue.text: Set meal and free bed at hotel

indicators.note: the letters are set free into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A hotel offers a fixed menu and a free bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like no charge, but signals rearranging BEDATHOTEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A French term for a fixed-price menu with set courses.

clue.text: Trials from which the public are excluded

definitions.text: Trials from which the public are excluded

parts.words: Trials from which the public are excluded
parts.note: sounds like court cases in camera, but means practice runs before the audience is let in

explanation.surface: Court hearings held behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trials' suggests courtrooms; these are trial runs of a play before opening night.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre practice sessions are trial runs held before any audience attends.

parts.note: something growing at the centre of a children's game, which they circle singing a nursery rhyme

explanation.surface: A centre for children's play is growing.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme 'Here we go round...', children dance in a ring around this plant, so it is a growing thing at the centre of their game.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrub of the nursery rhyme stands in the middle of the children's circle game.

clue.text: Rise and fall of one of the French, recently deceased

parts.note: UN is French for one
DU is French for 'of the'
late means recently dead

explanation.surface: The rise and fall of a Frenchman who has recently died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' applies to both 'one' and 'of the'.
explanation.definitionFit: To undulate is to move up and down in waves.

clue.text: At university, eccentric master is against the current trend

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters are oddly arranged

explanation.surface: An odd teacher at university resists what is fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges MASTER into STREAM; UP is British for being at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Going against the current of a river, or figuratively of a trend, is moving this way.

clue.text: Anti-royalist has a bit of a fight getting capital

parts.note: a round is one section of a boxing bout
capital means head, from Latin caput

explanation.surface: A republican takes part in a fight to win the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Roundheads were Parliament's supporters against King Charles I in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of Parliament fought the king's party in the English Civil War.

definitions.meaning: to raise up or improve, morally or materially
a bra that lifts and supports the bust

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on bras that raise the bustline.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means raising spirits or conditions, and also support given by a bra.

parts.note: Pa is Dad, plus the S of the possessive
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: Rations for the Home Guard of the old TV comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a British TV comedy about the Home Guard; here it is Pa's TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian dough products such as spaghetti are a staple food.

parts.note: a verb meaning measures depth that is pronounced like the name of a stone fruit

explanation.surface: Something seems rich and mellow in tone.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means 'sounds' as in measures water depth, and it is pronounced like a fruit, so it also sounds fruity.
explanation.definitionFit: To plumb is to sound the depth of water with a weighted line.

clue.text: She robbed her sleeping partner of his capital assets

definitions.text: She robbed her sleeping partner of his capital assets

parts.words: She robbed her sleeping partner of his capital assets
parts.note: the biblical woman who cut the hair from Samson's head while he slept

explanation.surface: A businesswoman defrauds a silent partner of his money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleeping partner' and 'capital assets' sound financial, but mean a lover asleep and the hair on his head, the source of Samson's strength.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible she betrayed Samson by having his hair shorn as he slept.

clue.text: Top deck on old ship lacking lights

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece written on top of the next
the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: Noah's ark is an ancient ship

explanation.surface: The upper deck of an old vessel has no lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Without any lights, a place is unlit and so without brightness.

parts.note: a word for settling or levelling scores that also means paying someone off

explanation.surface: Someone settles a contest by paying off an official.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means levels the score, and informally also bribes someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both levelling a contest and, informally, buying someone off.

indicators.note: rearing up in a down clue means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: auks are smaller seabirds

explanation.surface: A big bird raising its young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearing' suggests raising chicks but means turning AUKS upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This large predatory seabird of the gull family harasses others for food.

clue.text: About due for a dockyard job

parts.note: re means about or concerning
fit means proper or due

explanation.surface: A ship due in the docks for work.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships go into the dockyard to be repaired and re-equipped.

clue.text: Sort of sketch one won't want to go under the hammer

definitions.text: one won't want to go under the hammer
definitions.meaning: the fingertip nobody wants to hit with a hammer

explanation.walkthrough: 'under the hammer' suggests an auction, but means literally being hit by a hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rough drawing, and the nail on the digit most at risk when hammering.
